title: P300 dataset BI2015b from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 44 subjects playing 'Brain Invaders', a visual P300-based Brain-Computer Interface videogame using an oddball paradigm on a 36-symbol grid. Recordings were made with 32 wet electrodes at 512 Hz sampling rate across three conditions with different flash durations (50ms, 80ms, 110ms), including resting-state and eyes-closed periods before and after game sessions. The dataset supports research on P300 event-related potentials and real-time adaptive Riemannian classification methods for BCI applications.
methods_description: EEG was recorded using a g.USBamp amplifier (g.tec) with 32 wet Silver/Silver Chloride electrodes in a 10-10 montage, referenced to the right earlobe with ground at Fz, at a sampling rate of 512 Hz with no online digital filtering. Event tagging was synchronized via a USB digital-to-analog converter connected to the amplifier's trigger channel to reduce jitter compared to software tagging. The paradigm involved three game sessions of 9 levels each with different flash durations (110ms, 80ms, 50ms), using pseudo-random flashing of groups of six symbols among 36 aliens to elicit P300 responses, with a real-time adaptive Riemannian Minimum Distance to Mean classifier used for online feedback.
